sections.skill: Identify the unstated assumption an argument needs and evaluate competing explanations

questions.prompt: An assumption is an unstated statement an argument relies on. A bridging assumption is one that, if added, makes the conclusion follow with certainty; a supporting assumption makes a prediction or explanation more likely. "The school's robot passed every test in the lab, so it will work at the competition." Which assumption most supports this prediction?

choices.text: The robot failed some tests last year.
The robot was built by students.
Conditions at the competition are like those in the lab.
Other teams also tested their robots.

questions.correct_answer: Conditions at the competition are like those in the lab.

questions.prompt: An assumption is an unstated statement an argument relies on. A bridging assumption is one that, if added, makes the conclusion follow with certainty; a supporting assumption makes a prediction or explanation more likely. "Mia's plant grew faster after she moved it to the window, so sunlight made it grow faster." Which assumption would most strengthen this explanation?

choices.text: The plant was watered and kept as warm as before the move.

questions.correct_answer: The plant was watered and kept as warm as before the move.

questions.prompt: An assumption is an unstated statement an argument relies on. A bridging assumption is one that, if added, makes the conclusion follow with certainty; a supporting assumption makes a prediction or explanation more likely. "Every member of the chess club is in grade 10. Jo is in grade 10. So Jo is in the chess club." This argument would become valid if we add the assumption "Everyone in grade 10 is in the chess club."
questions.correct_answer: True

questions.prompt: The cafeteria sold fewer sandwiches this week than last week. Which explanation is best supported if we also learn that the cafeteria was closed on two days this week?

choices.text: Fewer students attend the school this year.
The cafeteria was open on fewer days to sell sandwiches.

questions.correct_answer: The cafeteria was open on fewer days to sell sandwiches.

questions.prompt: An assumption is an unstated statement an argument relies on. A bridging assumption is one that, if added, makes the conclusion follow with certainty; a supporting assumption makes a prediction or explanation more likely. "This bridge is safe because it has stood for 80 years." A major change in how the bridge is used could weaken this argument.
questions.correct_answer: True

sections.skill: Find the gap between premise and conclusion
sections.relationship: Students choose statements that are true or related instead of ones the argument needs. Looking for the gap between what is given and what is concluded points straight to the assumption.
sections.author_note: Students choose statements that are true or related instead of ones the argument needs. Looking for the gap between what is given and what is concluded points straight to the assumption.

lesson.title: Find the gap between premise and conclusion
text: Write the premise and the conclusion side by side.
Find a word or idea in the conclusion that the premise never mentions, or a jump from "some" to "all" or from "then" to "now".

A bridging assumption closes the gap completely: with it added, the conclusion follows with certainty. A supporting assumption only makes the conclusion more likely. A necessary assumption is one the argument cannot do without: if it were false, the argument would fall apart.

example.title: Worked example (a different argument)
prompt: "Leo practiced piano every day this month, so he will win the recital prize."
steps: Gap: daily practice to winning the prize.

A supporting assumption: daily practice makes Leo play better than the other players. It makes the prediction more likely but does not make it certain, and Leo could also win for other reasons, so it is not strictly necessary.

questions.prompt: An assumption is an unstated statement an argument relies on. A bridging assumption is one that, if added, makes the conclusion follow with certainty; a supporting assumption makes a prediction or explanation more likely. "Sam is taller than Ana, so Sam is taller than Raj." Which assumption fills the gap?

choices.text: Sam is the tallest in his class.
Ana is at least as tall as Raj.

questions.correct_answer: Ana is at least as tall as Raj.

questions.prompt: An assumption is an unstated statement an argument relies on. A bridging assumption is one that, if added, makes the conclusion follow with certainty; a supporting assumption makes a prediction or explanation more likely. Every true statement about the topic of an argument is an assumption that the argument needs.
questions.correct_answer: False

questions.prompt: An assumption is an unstated statement an argument relies on. A bridging assumption is one that, if added, makes the conclusion follow with certainty; a supporting assumption makes a prediction or explanation more likely. "The park was crowded on Saturday, so it will be crowded this Saturday." What is the gap?

choices.text: From the park to the city
From one past Saturday to a future Saturday

questions.correct_answer: From one past Saturday to a future Saturday

questions.prompt: An assumption is an unstated statement an argument relies on. A bridging assumption is one that, if added, makes the conclusion follow with certainty; a supporting assumption makes a prediction or explanation more likely. If an assumption an argument needs turns out to be false, the conclusion no longer follows from the premises.
questions.correct_answer: True

questions.prompt: An assumption is an unstated statement an argument relies on. A bridging assumption is one that, if added, makes the conclusion follow with certainty; a supporting assumption makes a prediction or explanation more likely. "All squares are rectangles, so all rectangles are squares" needs no assumption to be valid.
questions.correct_answer: False

sections.relationship: Harder: facts that support or undercut an explanation.
sections.label: ADVANCED APPLICATION

questions.prompt: Claim: "Students who eat breakfast score higher on tests, so eating breakfast raises test scores." Which fact would most WEAKEN the claim?

choices.text: Students who eat breakfast also sleep more, and sleep is linked to higher scores.

questions.correct_answer: Students who eat breakfast also sleep more, and sleep is linked to higher scores.

questions.prompt: Claim: "The new crosswalk signal reduced accidents at Elm Street." Which fact would most STRENGTHEN the claim?

choices.text: The signal cost a lot of money.
Elm Street is near a school.
Accidents did not drop at similar streets that did not get the signal.

questions.correct_answer: Accidents did not drop at similar streets that did not get the signal.

questions.prompt: An assumption is an unstated statement an argument relies on. A bridging assumption is one that, if added, makes the conclusion follow with certainty; a supporting assumption makes a prediction or explanation more likely. "No reptiles have fur. This animal has fur. So this animal is not a reptile." This argument needs an unstated assumption to be valid.
questions.correct_answer: False

questions.prompt: An assumption is an unstated statement an argument relies on. A bridging assumption is one that, if added, makes the conclusion follow with certainty; a supporting assumption makes a prediction or explanation more likely. "Our team lost every game we played in the rain. It will rain on Friday. So we will lose Friday's game." Which assumption most supports carrying the past pattern forward to Friday?

choices.text: It rains more in the spring.
Our team has played in the rain before.
Friday's game will be like those rainy games in the ways that mattered.

questions.correct_answer: Friday's game will be like those rainy games in the ways that mattered.

questions.prompt: Two explanations both fit the facts. Then no new fact can help decide between them.
questions.correct_answer: False

sections.relationship: Expert: alternative explanations and hidden assumptions.
sections.label: EXPERT CHALLENGE

questions.prompt: A town's ice-cream sales and its number of sunburns rise and fall together during the year. Which explanation is best?

choices.text: Sunburns make people buy ice cream.
The two numbers match by chance every year.

questions.correct_answer: Hot, sunny weather increases both.

questions.prompt: An assumption is an unstated statement an argument relies on. A bridging assumption is one that, if added, makes the conclusion follow with certainty; a supporting assumption makes a prediction or explanation more likely. "Ming read the book, so Ming knows how it ends." Which assumption best supports this inference from Ming's reading?

choices.text: Ming read the book all the way to the end.
The book has a surprise ending.

questions.correct_answer: Ming read the book all the way to the end.

questions.prompt: An assumption is an unstated statement an argument relies on. A bridging assumption is one that, if added, makes the conclusion follow with certainty; a supporting assumption makes a prediction or explanation more likely. "Every prize winner practiced daily. Kai practiced daily. So Kai won a prize." Adding "Only prize winners practiced daily" makes the argument valid.
questions.correct_answer: True

questions.prompt: A survey of the chess club finds that 90% of members prefer quiet study rooms. A student concludes that 90% of the whole school prefers quiet study rooms. What assumption does this need?

choices.text: The survey asked about study rooms.
The chess club has more than 10 members.
Chess club members have the same preferences as the whole school.
Quiet rooms are better for studying.

questions.correct_answer: Chess club members have the same preferences as the whole school.

questions.prompt: If a needed assumption is shown to be false, the conclusion of the argument must be false.
questions.correct_answer: False
